notes: Machine-readable contract for the peer-to-peer Dimension sync model: hashgraph-style gossip between players who share map regions, once-per-turn sync inside a Dimension, and a once-per-interval Radicle git push as the only (decentralized) central point. Every entry is a VersionedEntry so the protocol parameters themselves are voteable.

versions.notes: Derived from Rule 14 Part C (8-neighbour adjacency) and the author's region concept: players in strongly referenced regions share the same turn state and handshake every action; players that can reach each other within one real-time sync interval share the same map hashgraph to avoid collisions on first contact; far players sync once per turn or only at the Radicle push.

tiers.label: Contact region
tiers.membership: players/creatures whose tiles are adjacent or within strong_radius_tiles of each other, or that currently target each other (attack/move/follow)
tiers.consensus: every action is a signed hashgraph event; the action resolves only when all strong-region members have gossiped it (virtual voting, no leader)
tiers.failure_mode: a member that does not answer the handshake within handshake_timeout_s is treated as playing Empty Posture for that action (rule_6) and marked lagging

tiers.label: One-interval reach region
tiers.membership: players that could enter each other's strong region before the next Radicle push (max move distance x actions x rounds per radicle_push_interval_s)
tiers.consensus: members exchange a signed TurnCommit at the end of each turn so that the shared map hashgraph is identical before any first contact
tiers.failure_mode: missing commits are filled on first contact via hashgraph merge (see sync_divergence_merge)

tiers.label: Unmet / distant region
tiers.membership: everyone else inside the Dimension, including clans and new players that have never met
tiers.consensus: none in real time; the Radicle branch ActiveDimensions/<DimensionName>/ is the eventual rendezvous point
tiers.failure_mode: state is allowed to diverge; divergence is reconciled on first contact or at the next push

data.tier_promotion: a far/reachable peer is promoted to strong as soon as a position event places it inside strong_radius_tiles; promotion triggers a full state handshake (sync_join_flow step adopt_hashgraph_part)

logic.description: Governs which peers of a Dimension share live turn state (strong), which only share the map hashgraph (reachable) and which merely share the descriptor (far). Tunables: tiers[0].strong_radius_tiles (2) is the hex distance at or under which two live units are strong-region members; the reachable tier has no number of its own, its reach_tiles is derived as move_tiles_per_action(1) x actions_per_round(3) x turns per radicle_push_interval_s. The runtime (peer.mjs) deviates: STRONG_RADIUS defaults to 2*EM_MAX_STEPS+2 = 8 axial hexes (not 2 tiles on an 8-neighbour grid), REACH_RADIUS is STRONG_RADIUS + reveal radius (10) = 18, a member must also be alive and heard from within the last 20 s, the strong set is recomputed every action and frozen at commit (no full-state handshake on promotion), and every reveal the peer holds is resolved whatever tier its actor is in; members that did not reveal are resolved from their last published snapshot. Battle context assumed: a / b = units with tile {q,r}, life, target, tier, last_seen_age_s; me, peers = my unit and the live roster; region.reach_tiles = the derived reach; runtime.em_max_steps.

prerequisites.description: Two units are strong-region members when their hex distance is at or under tiers[0].strong_radius_tiles, or when either currently targets the other.
Only living units count as region members; the runtime additionally drops a peer whose last snapshot is older than 20 s (contract is silent on liveness).

effects.description: reach_formula: 1 tile per action x 3 actions per turn x turns per Radicle push interval (radicle_push_interval_s / clock.turn_seconds, floored).
The tier name of unit b relative to unit a: strong when within the strong radius, reachable when within region.reach_tiles, far otherwise (peer.mjs tierOf).
Unit b is in a's reachable tier: outside the strong radius but within region.reach_tiles.
Ids of the live peers within the strong radius of me — the set the handshake waits for and the state hash covers (peer.mjs computeStrongMembers).
tier_promotion: a peer not yet strong is promoted the moment a position event places it inside the strong radius.
Deviation: peer.mjs derives its strong radius from movement, 2*EM_MAX_STEPS+2 (8 with the default 3 Empty-Move steps), instead of the contract's 2 tiles.
Deviation: peer.mjs reach radius = strong radius + reveal radius (default 10), not the move x actions x turns formula.

validation.description: Exactly the three tiers strong / reachable / far, each once.
tiers[0] is the strong tier, synced per action, with an integer strong_radius_tiles between 1 and 9 (it must stay under the 10-hex view radius so the reachable ring is wider than the strong disc).
Every tier syncs by handshake_per_action, turn_commit or radicle_push and names at least one shared_state item.
tier_adjacency and tier_promotion stay documented strings.

versions.notes: Mirrors the paper's simultaneous action rule (Rule 7) and the declaration sequence (Rule 8). Commit/reveal keeps face-down cards secret until everyone in the strong region has committed.

phases.name: commit
phases.payload: hash(action_card + effects + skills + salt) per actor

phases.name: reveal
phases.payload: the plaintext declaration + salt; peers verify the hash

phases.name: instants
phases.payload: optional Skills/instants/class abilities/point-buy responses, same commit-reveal in a mini-round

phases.name: evaluate
phases.payload: each peer runs the deterministic resolver (battle_system_core) locally and signs the resulting state hash

phases.name: finalize
phases.payload: action event is final when the state hashes of all members match; mismatch -> dispute (see sync_divergence_merge)

data.dice: D6 rolls (Rule 5 monsters, point buy) are produced by combining every member's revealed salt: roll = 1 + (sha256(concat(salts) + roll_index) mod 6). No peer can bias the roll alone.
data.monster_control: The monster's actions are generated by the peer that currently controls it per Rule 3, but the dice come from the shared salt so the result is verifiable by all.
data.transport_for_now: plain JSON messages over the P2P channel (WebRTC data channel or Radicle node link); binary encoding is a later optimisation

message_envelope.type: string (one of the ids in hashgraph_events.json)
message_envelope.self_parent: hash of the actor's previous event
message_envelope.other_parent: hash of the most recent event received from another peer
message_envelope.signature: detached signature over the whole envelope minus signature

logic.description: Governs the five-phase commit / reveal / instants / evaluate / finalize handshake every strong-region action goes through. Tunables: handshake_timeout_s (30) is how long a member may stay silent before it is deemed to play Empty Posture and marked lagging; max_retries (2) bounds dispute replays; phases[].all_members_required says which phases block on the whole strong set. Dice are specified as 1 + (sha256(concat(all members' salts) + roll_index) mod 6). The runtime deviates: peer.mjs runs three phases (planning -> reveal -> resolution); instants, point-buy destroys and class abilities ride inside evt_action_reveal, and finalize is just an evt_state_hash whose mismatch is logged, never disputed. The caps are COMMIT_WAIT_MS 800 / REVEAL_WAIT_MS 1500 with a hard cap of 2 x ROUND_SEC (12 s), not 30 s; a member still inside its own planning window is never timed out. Dice are derived from the ACTING peer's own salt only (effects.mjs rollDice over sha256(salt:purpose:action)), the signature is a stub string, the envelope carries extra state and _hash fields, and a reveal is never checked against its commitment. Context assumed: phase, elapsed_s, attempt, region.strong (ids), seen (ids), commits_seen, reveal.recomputed_commitment, commit.commitment, salt_digest_int, clock.round_seconds.

prerequisites.description: A blocking phase advances when every strong-region member has sent its envelope, or the handshake timeout has elapsed (stragglers become Empty Posture).
Only envelopes from members within the strong radius of sync_region_tiers are waited for.
A reveal is only accepted from an actor whose commit for the same action was seen (phase 1 before phase 2).

The sha256 recomputed over the revealed plaintext + salt must equal the committed hash (json-logic cannot hash; the runtime supplies reveal.recomputed_commitment). peer.mjs does not perform this check.
A dispute replay may run while the attempt counter is at or under max_retries.

effects.description: Number of handshake phases per action (5 in the contract, 3 in peer.mjs).
Names of the phases that require every strong-region member.
failure_mode: a member silent past handshake_timeout_s is resolved as Empty Posture (EP); null while the window is still open.
max_retries minus the attempts already made, floored at 0.
Shared-salt D6: 1 + (digest mod 6), where salt_digest_int is sha256(concat(salts) + roll_index) read as an integer (supplied by the runtime). peer.mjs seeds from the actor's salt alone.
Deviation: peer.mjs never waits longer than 2 x ROUND_SEC (12 s by default) for a silent member, instead of handshake_timeout_s.

validation.description: handshake_timeout_s is a positive number of at most 300 s.
max_retries is an integer from 0 to 10.
The phase list keeps its length, starts with commit then reveal (secrecy of face-down cards), and every phase flags all_members_required as a boolean.
message_envelope keeps exactly the canonical field set (hashgraph_events are wrapped in it).
The envelope always carries type, ids, clock, parents, payload, timestamp and signature.

versions.notes: Players who do not share a strong region do not need every action; they need the turn boundary so turn counters stay aligned and the map hashgraph stays mergeable.

data.when: after the last action of a turn is finalized in the player's strong region (or after Empty Posture when alone)

payload.region_state_hash: hash of the strong region's finalized state
payload.map_delta: list of tile changes since previous TurnCommit (revealed tiles, token changes, owner changes, new permanents)
payload.hashgraph_head: hash of the latest finalized event

data.turn_counter_rule: a Dimension-wide turn is the max turn seen; peers that are behind receive the missing TurnCommits before acting (they cannot skip turns, see rule_6 for Empty Posture catch-up)
data.far_region_notification: when a TurnCommit or Radicle poll reveals previously unknown map items (new clans, new DoorIds, long-distance permanents) the client raises the disturbance_in_the_force UI event and applies the delta to unrevealed tiles only

logic.description: Governs the once-per-turn TurnCommit that keeps reachable / far peers' turn counters and map hashgraph mergeable. Tunables: gossip_fanout (3) peers per hop and gossip_ttl_hops (6) hops bound the gossip; turn_counter_rule makes the Dimension turn the maximum seen, and a lagging peer forfeits the skipped actions as Empty Posture. The runtime deviates: every peer emits its own evt_turn_commit at the turn boundary (endRound) over libp2p gossipsub only (fanout / ttl are gossipsub's, not these numbers), the payload has no map_delta (map blocks travel in evt_map_sync / evt_map_extend) and positions are axial q,r; catchUpClock applies the max-turn rule every 100 ms with two guards: one action behind while mid-handshake never jumps, and one action behind while planning jumps only if a STRONG-region member is already ahead (a far explorer must not pace the dimension). Context assumed: turn, round, action, action_finalized, phase, peers[] with action/turn/id/tier, region.strong, dimension.max_turn_seen / max_action_seen, clock.rounds_per_turn, hops.

prerequisites.description: A TurnCommit is emitted after the last action of the turn is finalized in the strong region.
TurnCommits are for members that do not share our strong region (reachable or far); strong members already hold every action.
turn_counter_rule: a peer may act only when its turn equals the Dimension-wide maximum; behind peers first receive the missing TurnCommits.

effects.description: The Dimension-wide turn: the maximum of my turn and every peer's turn.
Actions a lagging peer forfeits as Empty Posture when it catches up to the highest action seen.
How many peers one gossip hop forwards to: gossip_fanout, or fewer when fewer peers exist.
Hops a TurnCommit may still travel: gossip_ttl_hops minus hops taken.
Deviation (peer.mjs catchUpClock): jump when 2+ actions behind; when exactly 1 behind, only while planning and only if a strong-region member is already at action+1.

validation.description: gossip_fanout is an integer from 1 to 16.
gossip_ttl_hops is an integer from 1 to 32.
The TurnCommit payload keeps exactly the canonical key set.
turn, region_state_hash and hashgraph_head are what makes the commit mergeable; they must stay.

entries.name: Interval Radicle push (the single decentralized rendezvous)

versions.notes: The author's design: one random active player holding a DoorId pushes the merged DoorId.json every interval. Everyone else polls git. This is the only centralization point and it is itself a decentralized Radicle repo.

paths.rules_snapshot: ActiveDimensions/<DimensionName>/rules_snapshot_commit (commit hash of data/ used by this session)

pusher_election.method: deterministic lottery among the active members of the DoorId's hashgraph: pusher = member with min( sha256(peer_id + hashgraph_head + interval_index) )
pusher_election.fallback: if the elected pusher does not push within pusher_grace_s, the next-lowest hash pushes; duplicate pushes are harmless because the merge is additive

data.commit_content: doors/<DoorId>.json = { magnet_id, turn, hashgraph_head, members, map_summary (revealed tiles count, owned towers/crystals/mines), last_push_at } - see dimension_session.json for the exact shape
data.merge_policy: git merge on the branch is additive: doors/ files from different clans never conflict (one file per DoorId); dimension.json conflicts resolve to the higher turn counter
data.git_poll_effect: on poll, if a new/changed doors/<DoorId>.json is seen that is not in the local hashgraph, the client schedules a background reconciliation and raises disturbance_in_the_force

logic.description: Governs the interval Radicle push, the only rendezvous point. Tunables: radicle_push_interval_s (3600) between pushes, poll_interval_s (300) between git polls, pusher_election.pusher_grace_s (300) before the runner-up of the sha256 lottery pushes instead; paths name the files under branch ActiveDimensions/<DimensionName>. The runtime deviates substantially: RADICLE_PUSH_SEC defaults to 60 s (demo), there is NO lottery — every peer pushes its own doors/<peer_label>.json (door_version 2) plus a deterministic dimension.json into its own Radicle namespace (rad://<RID>/<NID>), so doors never conflict and the merge policy is a union by the reader (join.mjs); nobody polls git on a timer (doors are read at join time), rules_snapshot_commit is deleted as a leftover, and the explorer URL is broadcast to the UI. Context assumed: now_s, last_push_s, me.id, me.door_ids_held, door_id, lottery.winner / lottery.runner_up (argmin sha256, supplied by runtime), dimension.name, ours.turn.max_seen / theirs.turn.max_seen.

prerequisites.description: A push is due once radicle_push_interval_s have passed since the last push.
pusher_election: the lottery winner pushes; the runner-up pushes once pusher_grace_s have passed in this interval without a push.
Only a holder of the DoorId's hashgraph may be its pusher.

effects.description: floor(unix_time / radicle_push_interval_s) — the lottery and evt_radicle_push interval number.
Start of the next interval: (interval_index + 1) x radicle_push_interval_s.
How many git polls fit in one push interval (12 with the canonical numbers).
Unix time at which the runner-up may push: interval start + pusher_grace_s.
paths.door with the placeholders filled: ActiveDimensions/<DimensionName>/doors/<DoorId>.json.
paths.dimension_descriptor with the placeholder filled.
Deviation: peer.mjs writes one door per PEER, doors/<peer_label>.json, in the peer's own namespace.
merge_policy: a dimension.json conflict resolves to the higher turn counter.

validation.description: poll_interval_s and radicle_push_interval_s are positive and a poll is never longer than a push interval.
pusher_grace_s is positive and shorter than the push interval so the fallback can still fire inside it.
The branch and every path stay under ActiveDimensions/ (governance_branch_layout).
paths keeps the canonical artefact names (dimension_descriptor, door, rules_snapshot).

entries.name: Joining a Dimension (open / follow a friend / new location)

versions.notes: The DoorId behaves like a magnet URI: it names a hashgraph head and the peers that hold it, not a server. Three ways in: open a new Dimension, join a friend/clan (adopt their hashgraph part), or appear at a brand-new location from an old push.

steps: generate DimensionName/Id and the initial tileset per rule_0_setup (size by expected player count)
create the local hashgraph genesis event with rules_snapshot_commit
publish ActiveDimensions/<DimensionName>/dimension.json + doors/<first DoorId>.json to Radicle (the opening players now own the Dimension)
optionally register the DoorId in the Firebase directory for discovery only
pick ActiveDimensions/<DimensionName>/doors/<DoorId> of the friend or clan
connect to the pe= peers of the magnet and request the hashgraph part they hold (adopt_hashgraph_part)
verify the chain from genesis to hashgraph_head against signatures and the rules snapshot
enter on a free tile inside the friend's reachable region per rule_0_setup entry-point constraints (not adjacent to a non-ally; traps still resolve)
become a holder of that DoorId; you may now be elected as its Radicle pusher
pick a DoorId whose last push is older than the current interval (state is known to be stale)

allocate a fresh map region: extend the tileset by one block (same size as the initial tileset, rule_0_setup) adjacent to the existing bounds and seed it with traps/monsters/skills/classes per rule_0_setup
mint a new DoorId for the new region with its own hashgraph branch rooted at the pushed head
push doors/<newDoorId>.json immediately so active players learn about it on their next poll
play on the stale snapshot; reconciliation with the live clan happens on first contact (sync_divergence_merge)

data.leave_dimension: a LeaveEvent is gossiped; the character card stays on its tile as a map item until the next Radicle push records the departure
data.firebase_role: discovery/coordination only: list of DimensionNames with their Radicle repo ids and last push time. Never game state.

logic.description: Governs how a peer enters a Dimension: open_dimension, join_near_friend (adopt a DoorId's hashgraph part, enter inside the friend's reachable region, not adjacent to a non-ally) or join_new_location (a stale DoorId, a fresh map block the size of the initial tileset, a new DoorId). door_id_format is a magnet URI naming hashgraph head, repo and peers. The runtime deviates: peer.mjs picks the flow by alliance (player -> open_dimension, anything else -> join_near_friend) and never runs join_new_location; DOOR_ID is the env string 'door-primary' and doors are keyed by peer, not magnet URIs; join.mjs unions doors/*.json across namespaces and places 'nearby' or 'random'; join sync adopts the clock of the most-advanced live peer and a peer that lands mid-handshake sits that action out (rule 6); adopted_head is always null, class_id null, and no signature chain is verified. There is no Firebase directory. Context assumed: join.flow / join.entry_tile / join.door_id, me.alliance, peers[] with tile/alliance/life/action, friend.tile, region.reach_tiles, door.last_push.interval_index, interval_index, ref.phase, dimension.tileset.initial_size.

prerequisites.description: The requested flow is one of the entry's flows.
No living unit stands on the entry tile.
rule_0_setup entry-point constraint: the entry tile is not in contact with a living unit of another alliance.
join_near_friend: the entry tile lies inside the friend's reachable region.
join_new_location: the chosen DoorId's last push is older than the current interval.
door_id_format: the DoorId is a magnet URI with the urn:dim exact topic.

effects.description: Number of steps the chosen flow prescribes.
Join sync: the joiner adopts the clock of the most-advanced live peer (peer.mjs syncClockFromMesh).
Only planning is safe to join; landing mid-handshake means sitting the action out (rule 6 Empty Posture).
join_new_location extends the tileset by one block the size of the initial tileset.
Deviation: peer.mjs chooses the flow by alliance — player opens, everyone else joins near a friend.

validation.description: Exactly the three flows open_dimension / join_near_friend / join_new_location, each once.
Each flow lists at least one step.
door_id_format stays a magnet URI template naming the hashgraph head (xs=) and peers (pe=).
leave_dimension and firebase_role remain documented strings (Firebase is discovery only, never game state).

entries.name: Reconciling divergent map parts on first contact

versions.notes: Two clans that never met hold two hashgraph parts that may disagree about tiles neither has actually touched. Merge rules keep the game fair without a server.

data.trigger: a TurnCommit or position event places two peers from different hashgraph parts inside each other's reachable region, or a Radicle poll shows a new DoorId
algorithm: exchange hashgraph heads and find the common ancestor (the Radicle push both parts descend from)
replay both event sets in consensus order (virtual voting timestamps: median of received-times across members)
tiles touched by only one part: take that part's state as-is

tiles touched by both parts: apply the deterministic resolver turn by turn in consensus order; tokens that cannot both exist (two owners of one tower) go to the earlier consensus timestamp, the later owner's cards return to their discard pile
hidden/unrevealed tiles: keep the seed from the Radicle genesis so both parts reveal identical traps/monsters (rule_2)
turn counters: the merged region adopts max(turn); the lagging part plays Empty Posture for the skipped actions (rule_6)
emit a MergeEvent signed by all strong-region members; the merged part becomes one DoorId holder set (old DoorIds remain as aliases)
data.dispute: if the resolver hashes differ at any step, the minority peers replay with the majority's events; a peer that still differs after max_retries is marked desynced and must rejoin via join_near_friend
data.cheat_resistance: only signed events in a validated chain are replayed; a peer cannot introduce cards it never drew because draws (rule_10) are events with shared-salt randomness

logic.description: Governs reconciliation when two hashgraph parts that never met come into reach: find the common ancestor, replay both event sets in consensus order, take single-touched tiles as-is, resolve double-touched tiles by the deterministic resolver with the earlier consensus timestamp winning conflicting ownership, keep seed-derived hidden tiles, adopt max(turn), emit a MergeEvent; a peer still differing after sync_handshake_per_action.max_retries is desynced. The runtime deviates: peer.mjs performs no merge or replay — checkStateHash compares incoming evt_state_hash payloads entity by entity (tile and life) with its own and only logs 'STATE DIVERGENCE #n', never disputes or marks a peer desynced; evt_merge is never emitted; the only merge that exists is the grow-only union of map blocks (addMapBlock via evt_map_sync / evt_map_extend); hidden placement does derive from MAP_SEED as specified. Context assumed: a / b with hashgraph_head and tile, region.reach_tiles, merge.common_ancestor, mine.state_hash / theirs.state_hash, parts (a, b with action), tile.touched_by_a / touched_by_b, claim_a / claim_b {ts, owner}, attempt, compared[] of {mine, theirs} entity pairs.

prerequisites.description: trigger: two peers hold different hashgraph heads and are inside each other's reachable region.
Both parts descend from a known Radicle push (the common ancestor hash is a string).
The dispute branch applies only when the resolver hashes differ.

effects.description: The merged region adopts max(turn) of the two parts.
Actions the lagging part plays as Empty Posture to reach the merged clock.
Tiles touched by one part only keep that part's state; tiles touched by both go through the resolver.
Two owners of one tower: the earlier consensus timestamp wins; the loser's cards return to its discard pile.
dispute: a peer that still differs after max_retries replays is marked desynced and must rejoin via join_near_friend.
Deviation (peer.mjs checkStateHash): the number of entities both peers resolved whose tile or life differ — only these count as divergence, and they are logged, not disputed.

validation.description: The merge algorithm keeps at least five string steps (ancestor, replay, single-touched, double-touched, turn).
Some algorithm step adopts max(turn) — turn counters never go backwards on merge.
trigger, dispute and cheat_resistance stay documented strings.
